newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank hikes special advances rate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank hikes special advances rate.

text.p: The Dutch central bank said on Thursday it was raising its main money market rate, the special advances rate, by 10 basis points to 3.00 percent for a seven-day pact it will launch at tender on Friday.
Subscriptions to the new special advances pact will be open on Friday and allocations will be announced shortly afterwards.
The new liquidity pact will replace a seven-day facility of 4.64 billion guilders expiring on Friday.
The Dutch central bank said the rate rise was prompted by the guilder's weakness against the mark.
The 10 basis points hike brings the rate on special advances to three percent, in line with the German repo rate.
"We find the current mark rate compared to the guilder very high and this was the reason to raise the advances," the central bank spokesman said.
The guilder was quoted at 112.60 per 100 marks before the Dutch central bank raised the special advances.
